sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Union County, NC?
sections.html:
Union County Tax Administration does, and its Revenue Division collects the bills. The Revenue Division is at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 119, Monroe, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111-0038 and a phone line at 704-283-3848.

Valuation questions and appeals go to the Tax Administrator's Office at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 236, or 704-283-3746. Paying in person happens at the Tax Collector's office on the first floor of the Union County Government Center, Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

The county also collects property tax bills for ten municipalities: Fairview, Hemby Bridge, Lake Park, Marshville, Marvin, Mineral Springs, Stallings, Waxhaw, Wesley Chapel and Wingate. A house inside one of those towns gets one combined collection through the county office. Ask the county which office bills a parcel inside a town not on that list.

sections.h2: What is Union County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Union County is the fastest growing of the four counties compared on one Census page, with 267,674 residents in July 2025, up 12.4% from the April 2020 base. Its land area is 632.74 square miles, and it has 376.6 people per square mile.

Census QuickFacts shows a median value of owner-occupied housing units of $417,300 for 2020 to 2024, an owner-occupied rate of 81.6%, and median household income of $102,900. There were 95,683 housing units in July 2025 and 2,707 building permits issued in 2025. The median gross rent is $1,496.

  • Persons per household: 2.95.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 40.5% of adults 25 and older.
  • Foreign-born persons: 12.2%.
  • Mean travel time to work: 29.8 minutes.

Values in the county's last general reappraisal moved sharply, which is covered next.

sections.h2: What did the 2025 reappraisal change in Union County?
sections.html:
It raised total taxable valuation from $32.38 billion in 2021 to $60.05 billion as of January 1, 2025, an increase of 60.05%. The county's results page lists residential up 63.45% and commercial and industrial up 45.59%.

The county reports 114,182 parcels in 2025 against 104,057 in 2021, and a median home value of $403,000 against $293,377. Notices of new values went out in the first week of March 2025, formal appeals were heard from April through July 2025, and a deadline to file was May 28 that year. The tax rate was adopted with the June 2025 budget, and bills on the new values were mailed in August 2025.

For 2026, the county says it only sends a new notice when something changes on a property, such as new construction, an addition, demolition, a renovation, rezoning or an acreage change. The 2026 appeals window opened January 1 and closed when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned on May 6, 2026. North Carolina requires counties to reappraise every eighth year, so ask the office about the next scheduled year.

sections.h2: When are Union County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property tax is due September 1 and can be paid without interest through January 5. A mailed payment counts if the postmark is on or before January 5, and when that date lands on a weekend the deadline moves to the following Monday.

Interest is 2% for payments made January 6 through 31 and an additional three-fourths of 1% each month afterward, the county says. Registered motor vehicle tax is paid when you register or renew a plate, so it does not appear on the same bill.

sections.h2: How can I pay my Union County tax bill?
sections.html:
There are five routes listed on the county's page: mail, drop box, phone, online and in person.

  • By mail with the return envelope, or to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.
  • By drop box on Stewart St. Extension behind the Historic Post Office.
  • By phone at 1-855-497-0718.
  • Online through the county's payment link.
  • In person at the Tax Collector's office on the first floor of the Government Center.

If you are selling, pay or settle the current bill through your closing agent so the buyer receives a clean parcel. Ask the closer to request a payoff figure from the Revenue Division.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Union County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review by Tax Administration, and move to a formal appeal before the Board of Equalization and Review if you disagree. The county's appeal page says a staff appraiser reviews your evidence, mails a decision, and sends the case to the board if you return the form at the bottom of the decision letter.

The page describes the board as five citizens who hear your case and the staff's, and says it rules within 30 days. Included with the board decision are instructions for appealing to the North Carolina Property Tax Commission, and state law gives 30 days from the mailing of the board's notice, under G.S. 105-290.

Useful evidence listed by the county includes appraisals as of the revaluation date, sales of similar properties, photos of unusual damage and letters about septic limits from Environmental Health or a licensed soil scientist. The percentage of change since a prior assessment cannot be considered. Both the informal review and the formal appeal are free, and a lawyer is not required.

sections.h2: What state relief programs can lower a Union County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three programs exist in North Carolina, and an owner can use only one of them. They are filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9, not with the state.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value of a permanent residence, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled, with income under the limit of $38,800 for 2026 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: taxes limited to 4.0% of income if income is under the limit and 5.0% if income is over it up to 150% of it, which is $58,200 for 2026 (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Applications should be filed during the listing period, which runs from the first business day of January through January 31, and the assessor must take them through June 1 before the tax year. The circuit breaker needs a new application every year, and deferred taxes can become due if the owner sells or stops living in the home.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Union County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
The lien stays with the property. Under G.S. 105-355, a tax lien attaches on the date the property is to be listed, along with penalties, interest and costs. A buyer or lender will want it paid at closing.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county can bring a foreclosure action in the county where the property lies under G.S. 105-374. The sale is a public auction at the courthouse door, and someone redeeming before confirmation pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

For a quick sale, the usual path is simple: get the payoff figure from the Revenue Division, have the closer pay it from the proceeds, and keep the receipt. The seller also pays the deed excise tax at $1.00 for each $500.00 of value under G.S. 105-228.30, collected by the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When are Union County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 and can be paid without interest through January 5. Late payments carry 2% from January 6 to 31 and three-fourths of 1% for each month after.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Union County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Tax Collector's office on the first floor of the Union County Government Center, Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. The mailing address is P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 appeal window still open for Union County real estate?
faqs.a: No. The county says the 2026 window opened January 1 and closed when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned on May 6, 2026. Ask Tax Administration about later years.

faqs.q: Does Union County have a veteran property tax exclusion?
faqs.a: Yes, North Carolina excludes the first $45,000 of appraised value for qualifying disabled veterans, with no age or income limit. File with the county assessor on the state form.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax when I sell in Union County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the register of deeds before recording, at $1.00 for each $500.00 or fractional part of the value. Your closer should show the amount on the settlement statement.
